summary.headline: Consolidated revenue rose 7% to INR554 crores, but EBITDA fell about INR16 crores as Maldives diesel costs spiked; India grew 16% at INR74 crores.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 7% YoY to INR554 crores and consolidated EBITDA was INR205 crores at a 37% margin. The decline in EBITDA was attributed almost entirely to Maldives fuel and ancillary costs, which rose to INR38 crores from INR19 crores as diesel prices roughly doubled from pre-war levels in April-May. India delivered 13% revenue growth and 16% EBITDA growth, with occupancy and ADR both up. Reported PAT of INR124 crores was inflated by a INR102 crore deferred tax reversal following the tax regime switch.

financial_highlights.change: YoY decline of about INR16 crores
Broadly flat; about 3% growth adjusted for one-off transaction costs
Includes INR102 crore net deferred tax liability reversal from tax regime change; tax rate cut from 34.94% to 25.17%

financial_highlights.value: INR2,095 crores (India INR1,329 crores; Maldives USD81 million / INR766 crores)

segments.name: India hospitality
segments.commentary: Revenue INR203 crores (+13%) and EBITDA INR74 crores (+16%); occupancy rose about 7% to 67% and ADR about 8%, giving RevPAR growth of about 20%. Adjusted for a one-off electricity benefit in the prior year, EBITDA growth would be 18%.

segments.name: Maldives resorts
segments.commentary: Revenue INR218 crores (+5%) but EBITDA INR32 crores (-32%); fuel and ancillary costs rose to INR38 crores from INR19 crores. Excluding the fuel spike, management says EBITDA would have grown about 10%.

segments.name: Annuity (commercial/leased assets)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR128 crores (+3%) and EBITDA INR111 crores at 87% margin; committed occupancy 98%. Narmada Estates in Pune was recently added.

segments.name: Hospitality total
segments.commentary: Hospitality EBITDA declined 4% YoY to INR106 crores; adjusted hospitality EBITDA growth was about 14%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove simultaneous occupancy and ADR gains in India in a seasonally soft quarter, and is there headroom in Pune?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to Pune dominance (about 65% of luxury inventory), MICE, corporate demand in IT/BFSI micro markets and weddings; it expects Pune occupancy to stabilise in the high 70s and sees 200-300 luxury and upper-upscale room nights a day added from office growth.

qa_highlights.question: Where do India margins settle, and is there operating leverage beyond cost savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the solar capex (about INR60 crores, 3-year payback) could add roughly 4-5% to margin from Q1 next year, and that high occupancy is driving operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: What is Maldives demand doing in April-June, July and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: India source-market demand rose to about 9% from 6%; China and Russia grew at double-digit occupancy; July tourist arrivals were back to 2025 levels with only 27 disrupted flights versus about 170 earlier.

qa_highlights.question: How will the Sahyadri/Kelzai acquisition be funded, and what is the threshold for acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said funding will mix debt and internal accruals, with tourism incentive subsidies of 15-20% of capital expected and operations in about 2 to 2.5 years; debt to be drawn in stages as needed. The acquisition criteria answer was not captured clearly in the transcript.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Maldives EBITDA decline was diesel versus operations, and what is the FY27 margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline entirely to fuel: fuel bill up INR17 crores plus INR2 crores indirect, total about INR19 crores; ex-fuel Maldives EBITDA would have grown about 10%. Diesel was still about 20% below spot due to cluster procurement.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Goa Hilton performance and expansion timing and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said occupancy and revenue are improving post-acquisition (104 keys), gave no unit-level numbers, and said the 50-plus key extension and refurbishment are in planning, with delivery around FY29-FY30; it expects to conservatively double EBITDA with the pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Sri Lanka Arugam Bay commissioning moved from FY28 to around FY30?
qa_highlights.answer: Permissions are the constraint due to environmental sensitivity, about 1.5 km of shoreline and adjacency to Yala National Park; completions and formalities are near, with target around FY30.

qa_highlights.question: What are July and August trends for Maldives, and what do Q3/Q4 look like?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify August EBITDA margin, which depends on the war; it said occupancy remains strong and bookings on the books for Q3 and Q4 look very strong.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Maldives margin to recover as diesel prices ease and solar capacity comes online; Q3 and Q4 peak seasons expected to recoup the Q1 and Q2 fuel-driven decline (about INR15 crores impact).
Fuel costs in July were already about 26% below the April-May peak, per management.

India: solar capex (about INR60 crores, Pune) targeted for Q4 FY27 commissioning, expected to add 5-6% to India EBITDA (elsewhere cited as 4-5% margin increase); management expects margin uplift from Q1 next calendar year.
Maldives solar: Raaya to reach about 80% solar with battery backup by April 2027; expected savings about USD1.5 million a year (about 2.5% of Maldives EBITDA), with results from FY28.
Management expects to conservatively double India EBITDA over time after the pipeline and Goa expansion are delivered; Pune occupancy expected to stabilise in the high 70s.
Maldives July tourist arrivals reported as recovered to 2025 levels; management declined to give an August EBITDA margin view, which depends on the war situation.
capex_capacity: Captive solar plus battery storage at Pune hotels: about INR60 crores invested, commissioning targeted Q4 FY27, green share to rise from about 70% to about 85%, Pune energy bill expected to fall about 45%, payback about 3 years.
Raaya (Maldives) solar to rise from 1.2 MW to almost 5 MW, with additional capacity at Conrad and Anantara; no upfront capex per management.

Sahyadri Hills (Ritz-Carlton Reserve wellness estate, 80 keys plus 33 branded residences, ~425 acres) acquired 100% at equity consideration ~INR281 crores and EV ~INR466 crores; completed July 2026, occupancy certificate received, target yield-on-cost above 12%.

Pipeline of over 1,700 keys across 8 upcoming hotels: AC by Marriott Whitefield (Bengaluru), Varanasi Marriott, Ritz-Carlton Reserve Arugam Bay (Sri Lanka, 73 villas), and Soho House Delhi, progressing toward completion FY28 to FY30. Arugam Bay timeline slipped to around FY30 on permissions.

Promoter ROFO pipeline of 1,114 keys (JW Marriott Navi Mumbai and 3 Moxy hotels) cited toward a 4,000-plus key ambition; Goa Hilton (104 keys) brownfield extension of 50-plus keys in planning; Sol De Goa (21 boutique keys, Nerul) and Saipem Hills land in planning, delivery around FY29-FY30.
demand_pricing: India: occupancy up about 7% to 67% with ADR up about 8%, RevPAR up about 20%; management said occupancy and rate rose together, driven by Pune, Bengaluru and Goa demand, MICE, corporate and weddings.
Pune: management says it controls about 65% of luxury inventory, with no new luxury supply announced and a runway of 4-5 years; about 45 million sq ft of office stock expected to be added by 2030.

Maldives: revenue up about 5% despite April war-related cancellations; India source-market demand up from 6% to about 9%; China and Russia posted double-digit occupancy growth; mix shifting to direct, retail, loyalty and wholesale with higher-value source markets.
Annuity: revenue up 3% to INR128 crores, committed occupancy 98%.
Same-store revenue up 10% and same-store EBITDA up 15% in the quarter, per management.
risks_watch: Maldives fuel cost trajectory and the West Asia conflict: management says the Q3/Q4 recovery depends on diesel easing and the war situation, and it declined to give an August margin view.
Maldives Q3/Q4 recovery of about INR15 crores of lost EBITDA is assumed but not yet proven; monitor Maldives EBITDA margin in Q2 and Q3.
Execution risk on Sri Lanka Arugam Bay (permissions, environmental clearances, timeline slipped to around FY30) and on the 8-hotel pipeline (FY28-FY30).
Acquisition funding: Sahyadri Hills and the Sri Lanka build are to be funded partly by debt at about 7-8% cost; monitor net debt/EBITDA (1.2x) and the cost of funds (7.2% India, 6.1% Maldives).
Pune demand concentration: India growth rests on Pune and the 65% luxury share; monitor occupancy sustainability versus management's high-70s target.
Earnings quality: PAT of INR124 crores includes a INR102 crore deferred tax reversal; underlying PAT is much lower.
key_quotes: The pressure this quarter was on costs, not on demand.
So, if we look at the cost of Maldives EBITDA, it would have grown by 10% versus the -32% EBITDA decline in a non-peak quarter under war conditions.
We have acquired it 100% at an equity consideration of around INR281 crores and enterprise value of around INR466 crores, targeting a yield-on-cost above 12%.
So that is why I feel the pricing power in Pune will, is here to stay and strong.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on India demand and the long-term Maldives franchise, but guarded on Maldives near-term margins, which management tied explicitly to the war and diesel prices. Some answers were vague on specifics (acquisition criteria, August trends), and management gave no unit-level Goa numbers.
